summary: DONE is correct. Commit 60633eff3 implements the core of the proposal. The turn start forks a baseline wait before session preparation, so the wait overlaps the session start. It joins that wait, bounded at 5 s, before markDispatched and sendTurn. The CheckpointReactor now runs one keyed-serial lane per thread, and the turn-start baseline is a queued lane item, so it also waits for the previous turn's queued completion capture. That closes the follow-up-send variant the earlier verifier raised. sendTurn has only two callers: the turn-start path and the context-handoff path, and both join the baseline first. Layer wiring provides CheckpointReactor to the ProviderCommandReactor (PCR). The auditor missed two problems in the fix. (1) The Stop check (laneControl.failIfCancelled) runs before the new baseline join and nothing re-checks afterwards. A user Stop that arrives during the join (0-5 s, and usually the whole capture on a prewarmed or warm session) therefore no longer cancels the start. The turn is still sent, and the queued interrupt reaches the provider before the turn exists, so the Stop is lost. (2) On timeout the fix records a 'checkpoint.baseline.unconfirmed' activity with turnId null. The client work log hides turnId-null activities once a latest turn exists, and the turn's checkpoint status is never set to 'missing', so the timeout is effectively silent in the UI. Two minor uncovered paths remain. If the thread's recorded worktree is missing, the forked baseline sees a non-git cwd and reports success without capturing, before ensureSessionForThread recreates the worktree. The setup script also still writes into the worktree alongside the first-turn baseline, but the proposal did not cover that.

evidence.note: The baseline fork (`forkScoped(awaitPreTurnBaseline(threadId))`) starts before buildSendTurnRequestForThread (2086). That function reaches ensureSessionForThread (758), so the capture overlaps the session start as proposed.

DEFECT: `laneControl.failIfCancelled(turnFence)` runs at 2158, BEFORE `joinPreTurnBaseline` at 2159. Nothing re-checks cancellation before `retain`, `markDispatched` (2189) and the forked `providerService.sendTurn` (2166). Before 60633eff3 the check sat immediately before the send. `git show 60633eff3` shows the join was inserted after it.

Only `guardStart` registers a `currentStart` cancel Deferred (322). PCR uses guardStart only for session starts (896, 1121) and the handoff path (1852), so the baseline join is not cancellable by a noted Stop.

The interrupt lane item runs after the turn-start item has forked the send. cancelledAStart is false, so it calls providerService.interruptTurn (2433). That can run before the forked markDispatched and sendTurn reach the adapter. For example, ClaudeAdapter.ts:6194 has no turnState yet and just calls query.interrupt(). The turn then runs despite the Stop.
awaitPreTurnBaseline wraps `ensurePreTurnBaseline` in `timeoutOption(preTurnBaselineWait)`. The default is 5 s (252).
The timeout activity `checkpoint.baseline.unconfirmed` is appended with turnId null. No checkpoint status is set to 'missing'.
shouldIncludeActivityInWorkLog drops activities whose turnId is not the latest turn, so the turnId-null unconfirmed notice is hidden once the turn starts. No UI code references this activity kind.
makeKeyedSerialWorker keyed by inputThreadId (100) replaces the global drainable worker. Capacity is global (1024) but lanes do not block each other (packages/shared/src/KeyedSerialWorker.ts).

ensurePreTurnBaselineForTurnStart always enqueues a `baseline` item and awaits its Deferred. processInputSafely (1596-1613) always completes the Deferred, so the wait is ordered behind the thread's queued completion capture.

ensurePreTurnBaseline checks the knownCheckpointRefs memo, then hasCheckpointRef, then captureCheckpoint. If the thread's cwd is not a git repo yet (462), it returns as if it had succeeded. That happens when a missing recorded worktree is only recreated later in ensureSessionForThread (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:786).

streamEvents creates a fresh PubSub subscription per consumer. The reactor's runtime consumer (CheckpointReactor.ts:1657) only filters and enqueues, so in practice turn.completed is in the lane before a follow-up send can pass ingestion, the projection, PCR and a client round trip.
CheckpointReactorLive is provideMerge'd below ProviderCommandReactorLive, so PCR's serviceOption(CheckpointReactor) (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:449) resolves to Some.

runSetupProgram starts the project setup script before the turn start is dispatched. watchSetupScriptTerminal is forkDetach'd (ws/context/worktreeSetupProgress.ts:120), so the script still writes alongside the first-turn baseline. This was outside the proposal.

Tests cover holding the turn until the baseline lands and the late-baseline activity (4293). No test sends a Stop during the hold. CheckpointReactor.test.ts:638 and ~690 cover the queued-completion ordering and lane isolation.

fixDefects:
1. Stop regression (verified by reading the code). In prepareAndSubmitTurnStart, `laneControl.failIfCancelled(turnFence)` (ProviderCommandReactor.ts:2158) runs before `joinPreTurnBaseline(baseline, event)` (2159), and nothing re-checks before markDispatched (2189) and sendTurn (2166). A user Stop (session stop or turnId-less interrupt) noted during the join therefore does not cancel the start. The join can take up to 5 s. On a prewarmed first turn or a quick follow-up it is the whole capture, roughly 0.1-1.7 s. The interrupt's lane item then runs before the forked send reaches the provider, interrupts nothing (no turnState yet), and the turn runs anyway. Before the fix this window was essentially zero.

2. The timeout is not visibly recorded. The `checkpoint.baseline.unconfirmed` activity has turnId null (1979), and the client work log filters it out once a latest turn exists (session-logic.ts:940). Nothing marks the turn's checkpoint as 'missing'. The proposal's 'record checkpoint status missing' is therefore only a server log plus a hidden activity.

3. Missing-worktree path (minor). The baseline is forked before ensureSessionForThread recreates a missing recorded worktree (786). resolveCheckpointCwd then sees a non-git cwd (CheckpointReactor.ts:462), and the join reports success without a capture. On that thread's first turn the baseline still races the agent through the runtime turn.started fallback.

Out of scope, noted for completeness: the setup script runs alongside the first baseline (ws/context.ts:1016). Separately, a pre-existing and unrelated Codex issue: turn.diff.updated fires mid-turn, and ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:3119 creates a placeholder for it that CheckpointReactor.captureCheckpointFromPlaceholder (CheckpointReactor.ts:705) captures at once. The turn.completed capture is then skipped because a real checkpoint exists, so a Codex turn's ref N can be a mid-turn snapshot. This needs its own finding.
implementationSketch:
1. Stop fix, in apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderCommandReactor.ts prepareAndSubmitTurnStart. Make the join cancellable by wrapping it: `yield* laneControl.guardStart(turnFence, joinPreTurnBaseline(baseline, event))`. Interrupting a Fiber.join does not interrupt the baseline fiber, and the queued lane item still completes. The minimal alternative is to call `laneControl.failIfCancelled(turnFence)` again right after the join. Either way the cancellation surfaces as ProviderSessionStartCancelledError, and processTurnStartRequested -> reportTurnStartFailure -> settleCancelledTurnStart handles it. Skip appending the unconfirmed activity when the start was cancelled. Test in ProviderCommandReactor.test.ts, cloned from 'holds the provider turn until the pre-turn checkpoint baseline lands': hold the baseline, wait for startSession, dispatch a user thread.session.stop or a turnId-less thread.turn.interrupt, release the baseline. Assert sendTurn is never called, markDispatched is not recorded, no provider.turn.start.failed activity exists, and the session is settled as after a cancelled start.

2. Visible timeout (optional, low value). After sendTurn returns the turnId, attach the notice to that turn: dispatch the activity with the turn's id, or have CheckpointReactor mark the turn's checkpoint payload with a `baselineUnconfirmed` flag that the diff panel can show. Test that the activity survives deriveWorkLogEntries with the new latest turn.

3. Missing worktree (optional). Have CheckpointReactorShape.ensurePreTurnBaseline return a status ('ensured' | 'no-git-cwd'). When PCR gets 'no-git-cwd' and buildSendTurnRequestForThread then recreated the worktree, run awaitPreTurnBaseline again after preparation and before the join. Add a PCR test with a missing recorded worktree.

Setup-script gating and the Codex mid-turn placeholder capture belong in separate findings.
decisionReason: Server-local fix to turn-start ordering only. It does not touch auth, E2EE, Hub protocol or hosted lifecycle ownership.
correction: The auditor's DONE stands, but their fixDefects missed a regression introduced by the fix. The Stop/cancel fence check (failIfCancelled) still runs before the new, up-to-5 s baseline join and is not repeated, so a Stop during the join no longer cancels the turn start. They also called the timeout activity a visible record equivalent to 'status missing'. It has turnId null and is filtered out of the client work log once the turn starts, and no checkpoint status is set. Finally, they missed the missing-worktree path, where the forked baseline reports success without capturing because the cwd is not yet a git repo.
